lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.
- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations, raising inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5% within a year.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Cut inbound freight cost per pallet from $48 to $41 over two quarters by consolidating supplier pickups into four regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.

- Scoring 40 vendors weekly on on-time delivery, fill rate, lead-time variance and invoice accuracy, and sharing the scorecards with buyers before each quarterly review, raised on-time inbound deliveries from 81% to 93%.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Cut average route length from 120 to 90 miles, a 40% reduction, by solving the routing problem with customer time windows.
- Raised on-time deliveries by 9% in simulation, from 84% to 93%, by adding customer time windows to the routing model.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Wrote a slotting guide that the volunteer coordinators used to re-slot the warehouse again after its spring expansion.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Check that the contact details are real and working.
Make the profile link clickable and use its full destination.
items.because: The résumé may be viewed digitally.

items.says: Use consistent indentation and hanging indents for bullets.
items.because: A few bullets break across lines awkwardly and are harder to scan.

items.says: Consider putting Experience before Education.
items.because: Several years of relevant work may matter more to a reader than the degree.

items.says: Move Crestway Foods above Lakeview Distribution.
items.because: The jobs are not in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Add context for the daily delivery volume, such as its period or a service outcome.
items.because: It would establish the scale or quality of the work.

items.says: Keep the payment detail only if it supports the target roles.
Give the cooler-stocking work scale or operational impact, or prioritize the wedding-order work.
items.because: The cooler-stocking detail is less compelling without scale or responsibility.

items.says: Emphasize transferable operations responsibilities in the Greenleaf entry.
items.because: The job differs from the supply-chain roles.

items.says: Label the Greenleaf position temporary, seasonal, or part-time if applicable.
items.because: That context may help explain the transition.

items.says: Verify that the forecast-accuracy figures use a comparable scope and clarify what changed.
items.because: Changing which SKUs are included in MAPE can make the result look better without improving forecasts like for like.

items.says: Define whether the three-day and one-day figures are average, median, or another processing-time measure.
Give the scale of returns involved if possible.
Clarify your role in implementing the triage station.
Add the measurement period or basis of the average trailer wait.
items.because: That would make the comparison easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify what “locations” means and how the 2,000 were selected or counted.
items.because: Readers need to understand the scope of the result.

items.says: Clarify what the $1.9M reduction represents.
items.because: It could, for example, mean a reduction in average inventory.

items.says: Clarify the time period and attribution of the stockout and inventory results.
items.because: The bullet combines two reductions.

items.says: Add shipment volume or total savings if available.
Clarify the period used to compare the per-pallet costs.
Add a measured outcome for the reorder-point work.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibility but not impact.

items.says: Make the SKU scope consistent with the 1,400 SKUs mentioned above.
The bullet starts with an inconsistent verb form.
Clarify the timing of weekly scoring and scorecards shared before quarterly reviews.
Specify the comparison period for the 81% to 93% result.
Explain how vendor scoring contributed to the delivery result.
The stated OEE of 112% is not valid as standard OEE.
items.because: Standard overall equipment effectiveness cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: Show the guide’s adoption or a result from the forecasting workflow.
items.because: “The team still uses” is a vague outcome.

items.says: Confirm that the ongoing project date is accurate and the results reflect its current state.
A drop from 120 to 90 miles is 25%, not 40%.
The route-mile reduction conflicts with the 18% reduction in the first bullet.
items.because: The bullets may use different measures or baselines, but do not say so.

items.says: Reduce the overlap with the next bullet about customer time windows.
items.because: Each bullet should contribute distinct information.

items.says: The move from 84% to 93% is nine percentage points, not nine percent.
Make clear that the on-time result is simulated, not deployed.
Clarify whether the grocer supplied real data or the scenario or data are simulated or anonymized.
items.because: The project bullets could be read as real-world business results.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad first bullet.
items.because: It largely repeats the more specific work in the next two bullets.

items.says: Clarify whether the one-day improvement was measured or estimated and how it was verified.
items.because: The outcome sounds definite without showing how it was verified.

items.says: Explain how the process changes produced the one-day improvement.
Explain the slotting guide’s practical result or extent of use.
items.because: “Used to re-slot the warehouse again” is unclear.

items.says: Clarify what changed after the spring expansion.
Add other tools actually used, if applicable.
items.because: Excel and Python may be too narrow a list for this experience.

items.says: Add more specific methods or areas of expertise that you can discuss confidently.
items.because: The listed methods are broad.

items.says: Put the skills most relevant to the target roles first.
